newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Newmarket forecasts lower 1996/97 profit.
newsitem.headline: Newmarket forecasts lower 1996/97 profit.

text.p: Property company Newmarket Property Trust Ltd said on Thursday its June year profit would be materially below its original forecast.
The company forecast net profit after tax for the year to June 30 of NZ$1.857 million and $5.078 million for the June 1998 year.
Newmarket directors expressed disappointment in the financial performance of the trust to date.

"While the yield guarantee has preserved returns to investors (at 9.5 percent pre tax) the profit of the trust as at June 30 1997 will be materially behind that originally forecast," the company said.
This was mainly due to the rental income for the Rialto Centre being less than originally forecast.
Newmarket said it was likely that there would be writedowns in respect of both Rialto and the unsold units at George Court.

A re-evaluation of the George Court project showed a likely development loss. This arose from some reduction in net realisations achievable in the market and from the need to fit out units to achieve sales.
Newmarket said the trust in its present form was too small, and with George Court sold would effectively become a single property trust.
"We certainly believe that the trust needs and has the basic strength to expand, possibly by incorporating other properties and perhaps by expanding the capital base of the trust," the company said.
